children: shares fell 4.26% at 10:45 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, after the Commerce Department unveiled a rule that tightens how foundries and packagers handle advanced logic chips. Reuters reported that TSMC and Samsung shares lost ground in Asia as the measure raised due diligence and licensing burdens for foundries serving Chinese fabless companies.

The interim final rule keeps the presumption that certain advanced logic chips are controlled and narrows how fabricators can overcome it when the designer is located in, or headquartered in, a restricted destination. It adds a license requirement for such chips from designers that are neither approved nor authorized when a front-end fabricator or packager exports them. It also requires licenses for advanced chips sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, effective on publication scheduled for November 19.

For TSMC the likely cost is customer screening and slower approvals rather than lost leading-edge demand, since its biggest advanced-node customers are US designers such as Nvidia and AMD. Smaller Chinese design wins could still be delayed. GuruFocus gives TSMC a GF Score of 99/100, near perfect across profitability, balance sheet strength and momentum. Its GF Value of $383.04 implies a 4% discount, which GuruFocus rates fairly valued, so quality is priced in but not stretched. The next test is TSMC's November revenue report and any sign of license-related delays.

title: TSMC Stocks Fall 4.26% as New US Rule Tightens Checks on Chip Foundries
